#+title: The codegen tests write into the working tree
#+description: Running the codegen test suite leaves modified generated files behind: two files changed under a run of compass check, and neither is the branch's change. The gate that catches the resulting drift cannot then tell the side effect from the work.
#+type: capture
#+level: cross
#+filetags: 
#+created: 2026-10-16
#+updated: 2026-10-16

This page is a [[id:671F18E4-E09C-4B3B-BD24-D33DF8AE38A6][capture]] in the *inbox* bucket of the product backlog — a pre-sprint idea, not yet pulled into a sprint as a story.

* What

Make the codegen suite render into a temporary directory, or restore what it
touches, so that running a check never leaves the working tree different from
how it was found.

* Why

A run of `compass check` on a branch left two generated files modified that the
branch had not touched: `ores.refdata.api/domain/calendar_rule.hpp` and
`ores.reporting/core/tests/report_error_eventing_integration_tests.cpp`. The
first lost a paragraph of documentation that the model does not carry, so
committing it would have silently reverted a colleague's work. The second
gained two lines that no gate asks for.

Both were side effects of running the suite rather than the branch's change, and
`drift-sweep` passes with both reverted, which is how they were identified. That
takes a deliberate experiment to establish. A person who runs the checks, sees a
dirty tree, and commits what looks like their own work will merge someone else's
file back to an older shape.

The reason the experiment was needed is that the check that would catch drift
compares the working tree against HEAD, so it reports an uncommitted fix and an
uncommitted side effect identically.

* References

- `drift-sweep`, which renders every catalogue component and passed with both
  files reverted.
- The generated-file drift captures, which describe the same confusion between a
  hand edit and a render.
